benchmark_type_evidence: XGLUE not only includes these 5 existing tasks, but also introduces 6 new tasks selected from real-world scenarios (i.e., Search, Ads and News).
brief_description: XGLUE is a cross-lingual benchmark covering 11 tasks (both understanding and generation) across 19 languages, with English-only training data for each task. It includes 5 existing multilingual datasets and 6 new tasks from Search, Ads, and News scenarios.

CoNLL NER.annotation_quality_notes: Existing dataset from CoNLL-2002 and CoNLL-2003 shared tasks. 4 entity types: Person, Location, Organization, Miscellaneous. F1 metric.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: The XGLUE paper does not discuss the annotators of the UD Treebanks.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Universal Dependencies Treebanks contain native-language text for each language.

UDPOS.annotation_quality_notes: Existing dataset from UD Treebanks v2.5. ACC metric.

translated.evidence: We crawl this dataset from Microsoft News (MSN). News articles are natively written in each language.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: Labels are category labels from MSN, reviewed by human, but the paper does not state whether reviewers are native speakers.

culturally_grounded.evidence: News articles are crawled from MSN in each language, representing region-specific news content.

NC.annotation_quality_notes: New dataset. 10 news categories. Category labels from MSN website, human-reviewed. ACC metric.

translated.evidence: MLQA contains QA annotations labeled in 7 languages, natively created based on Wikipedia articles.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: The XGLUE paper does not describe the MLQA annotator demographics.

culturally_grounded.evidence: MLQA uses parallel Wikipedia passages across languages; underlying content is parallel/shared rather than culturally specific.

MLQA.annotation_quality_notes: Existing dataset. F1 metric. Data sourced from Wikipedia.

translated.evidence: We reuse the original XNLI dataset (Conneau et al., 2018). XNLI is a translation of the MultiNLI English corpus into 14 other languages.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: The XGLUE paper does not describe the XNLI translators.

culturally_grounded.evidence: XNLI is translated from English MultiNLI corpus, inheriting English-centric content.

translated.evidence: PAWS-X extends the Wikipedia portion of PAWS evaluation to more languages via translation.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: The XGLUE paper does not describe the PAWS-X translation process.

datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: 6 new tasks are constructed from Bing and MSN data natively sourced in each language without translating from English. Additionally, CoNLL NER, UDPOS, and MLQA are existing datasets with native-language data.

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: XNLI is translated from English MultiNLI corpus. PAWS-X extends English PAWS data via translation.

all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: The paper states labeling was done on 'an Microsoft internal crowdsourcing platform' with guidelines and tests, but does not specify whether annotators are native speakers of each target language.

creator_types_across_datasets: researchers (CoNLL, UD, MLQA, XNLI, PAWS-X original papers)
automated (QG es/it/pt via in-house QA ranker)
annotator_workforce.evidence: For tasks QADSM, WPR, QAM and QG, we label the data on an Microsoft internal crowdsourcing platform. Each labeler must learn the guideline and pass the labeling test. Each sample is labeled by three labeler.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: The benchmark is inherently English-centric by design: for all 11 tasks, training data is ONLY available in English. Models must learn from English training data and transfer to other languages (zero-shot cross-lingual transfer). 2 of 11 datasets (XNLI, PAWS-X) are direct translations from English.

notably_excluded: Sub-Saharan Africa (except Swahili in XNLI only)
geographic_representation.evidence: 19 languages total. Heavy concentration on European languages (de, es, fr, it, nl, pl, pt, ru, bg, el = 10/19). East/Southeast Asian: zh, vi, th (3/19). South Asian: hi, ur (2/19). Middle East: ar (1/19). East Africa: sw (1/19, only in XNLI).
